findings.title: PDF opening, rendering selection, text extraction and reflow already have dedicated paths
observed: ActivityTxt.pdfOpen2 constructs com.radaee.pdf.Document, calls Open, handles several failure codes and passes the document to PDFReader.open.
PDFReader.open selects PDFGLLayoutView or PDFLayoutView; setView also dispatches to distinct comic and DjVu layouts.

PDFReader.getPageText starts page objects, reads the character range with ObjsGetString and closes the page. ActivityTxt.pdfCreateReflowText passes extracted text and a page to format-specific formatting.
inferred: PDF rendering, extraction and reflow improvements should be described as extensions to existing capabilities.
unknown: Native implementation and exact Radaee SDK version, rendering fidelity, reading order, OCR coverage and performance were not established.

findings.title: PDF annotations have a persistence path whose status propagation needs verification
observed: PDFReader.pdfUpdateNotesToFile applies markup and popup text, marks annotations updated and calls save; selected calls are also visible in its smali.
ActivityTxt.pdfSaveChanges clears the dirty flag before PDFReader.save, then updates the saved-time and sync-state fields.
PDFReader.save returns void and calls Document.Save without consuming its boolean result.
inferred: A save-failure experiment should check whether the UI or synchronization state advances without a durable PDF write.
unknown: Actual write-failure behavior, native Save semantics and handling elsewhere remain unknown. pdfUpdateNotesToFile has decompiler warnings; its full reconstructed control flow is not treated as authoritative.

findings.title: Local notes and a reader-specific import/export format already exist
observed: BookDb.exportNotesToText queries the SQLite notes table by lowerFilename. NoteInfo carries book/file identity, chapter/split/position, original text, note text, time, highlight length/color and markup flags.

PrefChapters.doShare offers .mrexpt import/export. Non-PDF serialization contains a file-length header, formatting settings and delimited note records; PDF serialization uses a page-count header and separate tagged fields.
BookDb.importNotesFromText routes PDFs to PDFReader.pdfCreateNotesFromText; the non-PDF path reads positional records and recognizes deletion markers.
inferred: Interoperability work should build on existing export, while testing stable document identity, Unicode and format-version handling.
unknown: Round-trip fidelity and cross-version compatibility were not tested. PDF import has substantial decompiler warnings; non-PDF import also contains visibly imperfect reconstructed control flow.

findings.title: The .mrexpt export wrapper discards the write helper's boolean result
observed: BookDb.exportNotesToFile returns false for empty serialized content; otherwise it invokes T.saveFileText(String, String) and returns true without reading that helper's boolean result.
The smali confirms the boolean-returning invoke has no move-result before the unconditional true return.
The examined PrefChapters.doShare export callback chooses its success/failure message from exportNotesToFile.

Bounded follow-up: T.saveFileText(String, String) first calls saveNormalFileText; if that returns false it tries an SD DocumentFile output stream when applicable. Caught exceptions and exhausted or unavailable fallback lead to a false return.

T.saveNormalFileText(String, String) has a false-return branch when parent-folder creation fails and reconstructs direct FileWriter output with handled failure paths. The complex exception cleanup is imperfect Java reconstruction.

Together with the previously retained exportNotesToFile smali, this supplies a static chain from a helper's non-throwing false result to the wrapper's true result for nonempty serialized notes. The earlier uncertainty that the helper might only throw is resolved at the code-path level.
inferred: A failed direct write with no successful SD fallback can propagate as false from saveFileText, which exportNotesToFile discards. The examined export callback then has a path to its success message. This is a statically supported error-propagation concern, rather than a hypothesis based only on a boolean signature.
unknown: No destination failure was induced in the app. Android storage grants, file-picker acceptance, error-logging side effects and the exact visible result still require runtime verification on an authenticated build.

The ordinary writer's decompiled exception cleanup contains imperfect reconstruction; its full exception-flow semantics are not asserted from this Java output. The outer saveFileText false-return and exception-handling paths are the principal new evidence.

findings.title: Text, cover/image sharing and Readwise upload have separate implementations
observed: PrefChapters.createShareContent assembles checked highlights and notes with optional chapter headings; shareContent sends text/plain, optionally with a cover attachment.
For a constructed share string of at least 80000 characters, shareContent offers clipboard or text-file output.
PrefShareText.shareContent writes a cache filename ending .jpg but declares image/png in its share intent.
Readwise.addHighlights builds a token-authenticated JSON POST containing highlight text/title and optional author, note and chapter, with a result callback.
inferred: Sharing/export recommendations should distinguish the existing formats and destinations. The image filename/MIME pairing merits a compatibility check.
unknown: Actual encoded image type, receiving-app compatibility, Readwise endpoint availability and successful delivery were not observed. No credential values were extracted or published.

findings.title: Book search scans format-specific text using a compiled regular expression
observed: PrefSearch.startSearch stores the entered key and launches a worker that constructs Pattern from the key plus optional case-insensitive and word-boundary syntax; the worker smali corroborates this construction.
The Java reconstruction has separate plain-text, HTML/split, ebook-chapter and PDF branches. The PDF branch reads extracted or reflow text page by page.
Direction filters, result snippets, handler-based delivery and some result-count checks are present. stopSearch only clears inSearching; examined loops check that flag.
inferred: Test literal metacharacters, malformed regex, result-limit consistency and cancellation latency. Flag checks do not demonstrate interruption of an ongoing regex match or page extraction.
unknown: Intended regex UX, exception-state recovery, worst-case latency and all result-cap behavior remain unverified. startSearch has a decompiler type-inference warning; the smali check is limited to selected worker behavior.

findings.title: Cloud dispatch, reading-position exchange and compressed note synchronization exist
observed: Cloud.instance(int) selects Dropbox for 2, Google Drive for 4, FTP for 8 and WebDAV otherwise.

Sync.uploadCloudPositionFile serializes a stored position with a device identifier and optional extra field. notifyNewCloudPosition parses the payload, applies a same-device/manual rule, writes preferences and signals the reader.
Note upload uses BookDb.exportNotesToText plus deletion records and compression; note download decompresses, dispatches to the PDF or ordinary-note importer and invalidates reader views.
The examined exportNotesToText xref query returned two using methods: Sync.uploadCloudNoteFile and BookDb.exportNotesToFile.
inferred: Export and note synchronization share a serializer, making round-trip and compatibility checks relevant to both features.
unknown: Real authentication, server compatibility, transport behavior, retries, concurrent-device conflict handling and dynamic callers were not tested.

findings.title: Two examined file-freshness predicates reject equal-size files before comparing dates
observed: For an existing nonempty local file and a corresponding remote item, both cloudFileIsNewer and localFileIsNewer return false when byte sizes match.
For differing sizes, the predicates compare remote date and local lastModified; cloudFileIsNewer additionally rejects syncType 8. Both equal-size branches are confirmed in smali.

Bounded follow-up: each freshness-predicate xref query returned two using methods. cloudFileIsNewer is used by verifyDownloadBookCovers and a shared nested worker reported as Sync.7.1.run; localFileIsNewer is used by verifyUploadBookCovers and that same worker.

verifyDownloadBookCovers removes both local and remote cover-list entries when cloudFileIsNewer returns false, then calls downloadShelfBookCoversFinal. verifyUploadBookCovers removes corresponding cover entries when localFileIsNewer returns false, then calls uploadShelfBookCoversFinal.

The cover-verification xrefs each returned one callback: Sync.23.1.done for download and Sync.10.1.done for upload. These are JADX using-node identities, with no claim of complete dynamic call coverage.

The shared worker method could not be resolved using the containing-class identity supplied by the xref response. A separate resolve_class query for its reported numeric name also returned resolved=false; no body was obtained for that worker.
inferred: The equal-size early returns demonstrably gate the examined book-cover transfer lists in both directions. An equal-length changed cover represented in those lists is filtered out before the final cover-transfer call. A cover-refresh test is therefore the narrowest supported reproduction target.
unknown: The shared Sync.7.1.run worker's enclosing workflow remains unresolved. These results do not establish equal-size suppression for every book-file, reading-position or note-sync workflow.
Real cover-list construction, provider metadata correctness, cache invalidation and visible synchronization behavior were not exercised. Other transfer entry points may use different checks.

findings.title: Platform TTS is integrated with document text, selection, page progression and a foreground service
observed: ActivityTxt.initTTS constructs Android TextToSpeech; setSpeakQueue sets speech rate and pitch, queues identified utterances and optionally adds silence.
getSpeakText dispatches non-reflow PDF text to pdfGetTtsLines. That path uses extracted page text and character rectangles before A.getTtsLines.
Utterance progress callbacks update selection and trigger progression after the last utterance; doAfterAllUtteranceFinished advances or stops.
The manifest declares a non-exported BookTtsService with mediaPlayback type; its onStartCommand calls startForeground using the reader notification.
inferred: TTS proposals should target reliability, control and text segmentation improvements rather than introducing a capability already present.
unknown: Installed voices, speech-engine limits, audio focus, lifecycle robustness and actual spoken output were not tested.

findings.title: The queue submission method truncates an over-limit utterance
observed: ActivityTxt.setSpeakQueue compares each utterance string length with maxSpeechInputLength. If longer, it submits a substring ending at maxSpeechInputLength minus 10; the loop then proceeds to the next TtsLine. The branch is confirmed in smali.

Bounded follow-up: the saved A.getTtsLines reconstruction contains delimiter matching and TtsLine construction for segments, a whole input and a remaining tail. It also contains explicit JADX duplication warnings and inconsistent reconstructed conditions/catch variables; exact branching is not established by this Java output.

A.addTtsLine and the A.TtsLine constructor each have a surviving successful request/response pair with matching decoded sidecars in interrupted run E. Its original run.json still has calls=[] and no completion or post-run hashes; the two bodies are recovered response evidence, not evidence of a finalized run.
The recovered addTtsLine body checks isAvialable() and appends the same TtsLine object. That helper itself contains no length-based splitting. The availability helper's body was not selected.

The recovered constructor shows ruby/filter substitutions, whitespace processing and assignment of the stored text and offsets. Malformed reconstructed string literals and exception-flow variables remain despite Java mode and empty provider markers. These transformations are not a verified length bound.
inferred: The original smali-supported conditional concern stands: if an over-limit TtsLine reaches setSpeakQueue, its suffix is not submitted by that queue loop. The follow-up identifies relevant upstream stages but does not prove that an ordinary document produces such a line.
unknown: Exact segmentation branches, filter effects and the unselected isAvialable helper prevent a reliable end-to-end reachability conclusion from these saved Java reconstructions. No additional bytecode corroboration or application speech test was performed.

Run E lacks its final receipt, per-call timing, post-run input identity, unload acknowledgment and child-exit/cleanup result. Surviving response bytes and pre-run hashes do not supply those missing lifecycle facts.
Long unbroken text, user filters and engine limits still require a controlled runtime comparison of full input with spoken output on an authenticated build. No speech loss was reproduced.
